components.name: docs-templates-body
components.content:
> These docs describe Gazetta's `main` branch. The latest release on npm, 0.8.0, is older and works differently in places, and it lacks security fixes made since. To follow these docs, [run Gazetta from `main`](https://github.com/gazetta-studio/gazetta-studio#quick-start). # Templates A template is a TypeScript function that returns `{ html, css, js }`. Every template exports a Zod schema for its content — the CMS builds the editing form from it. Templates live at `templates//index.ts` (or `index.tsx` for JSX). ```ts // templates/hero/index.ts import { z } from 'zod' import type { TemplateFunction } from 'gazetta' export const schema = z.object({ title: z.string().describe('Page title'), subtitle: z.string().optional().describe('Subtitle text'), }) type Content = z.infer const template: TemplateFunction = ({ content }) => ({ html: `

${content?.title ?? ''}

${content?.subtitle ?? ''}

`, css: `.hero { text-align: center; padding: 4rem 0; } .hero h1 { font-size: 2.5rem; margin-bottom: 0.5rem; } .hero p { color: #666; font-size: 1.25rem; }`, js: '', }) export default template ``` ## The template contract The renderer calls the default export with a single params object: | Param | Type | Description | |-------|------|-------------| | `content` | `T`, optional | The component's content, validated against `schema` | | `children` | `RenderOutput[]`, optional | The rendered output of child components, in order | | `params` | `Record`, optional | Route parameters, on [dynamic routes](/docs/pages-and-fragments#dynamic-routes) | | `locale` | string | Active locale code (e.g. `'fr'`, `'en'`) — always provided by the renderer, defaults to the site's locale or `'en'` | The function returns a `RenderOutput` or a `Promise`. A template module exports only `default` and `schema` — the CMS generates the editing form from `schema`. To replace the form with a custom editor, add a separate file under `admin/editors/`; see [Custom editors](/docs/customize-editor#custom-editors). ## Template fields | Field | Type | Required | Description | |-------|------|----------|-------------| | `html` | string | Yes | HTML markup | | `css` | string | Yes | CSS (scoped per component automatically) | | `js` | string | Yes | Client-side JavaScript (`''` for static components) | | `head` | string | No | Content for `` — favicons, fonts, meta tags | The CSS scoping is automatic: the renderer prefixes every selector with a `[data-gz=""]` attribute selector and wraps the component's HTML in a matching container, so one component's rules don't leak into another. `head` bubbles up the tree: the renderer joins every child's `head` into the component's own, all the way to the page. Return only the tags this template adds — the children's tags arrive on their own, and collecting them again duplicates them in the final page. ## Frameworks Templates can use any framework that SSR's to HTML: **React** — save the template as `templates//index.tsx` and import React: `.tsx` templates are compiled with a JSX transform that needs React in scope: ```tsx // templates/card/index.tsx import React from 'react' import { renderToStaticMarkup } from 'react-dom/server' const template: TemplateFunction = ({ content }) => ({ html: renderToStaticMarkup(), css: `.card { padding: 1.5rem; }`, js: '', }) ``` **Vue 3** — needs `npm install vue` first; `init` doesn't install Vue: ```ts import { createSSRApp, h } from 'vue' import { renderToString } from 'vue/server-renderer' const template: TemplateFunction = async ({ content }) => { const app = createSSRApp(Quote, content ?? {}) return { html: await renderToString(app), css: '...', js: '' } } ``` **Interactive components** return JS that runs in the browser: ```ts const template: TemplateFunction = ({ content }) => ({ html: ``, css: `button { padding: 0.5rem 1rem; }`, js: `document.getElementById('btn').addEventListener('click', () => alert('Hi'))`, }) ``` ## Composite templates Layout templates receive `children` — the rendered output of child components. CSS and JS do not bubble: collect them from the children, or they never reach the page. `head` does bubble (see above), so a layout returns only its own additions: ```ts // templates/page-layout/index.ts import { z } from 'zod' import type { TemplateFunction } from 'gazetta' export const schema = z.object({ title: z.string().optional().describe('Page title'), }) type Content = z.infer const template: TemplateFunction = ({ content, children = [] }) => ({ html: `
${children.map(c => c.html).join('\n')}
`, css: `main { max-width: 800px; margin: 0 auto; } ${children.map(c => c.css).join('\n')}`, js: children.map(c => c.js).filter(Boolean).join('\n'), head: `${content?.title ?? ''}`, }) export default template ``` --- [Edit this page on GitHub](https://github.com/gazetta-studio/gazetta-studio/edit/main/docs/templates.md)
